title: Third-order failure constraints reduced mean half-loss uncertainty by 94 to 96 percent in two selected mouse contact models
abstract: We tested how third-order failure constraints change sharp half-weight-loss bounds in two published mouse contact sets. With failure probability 0.1 and exact pairwise independence, adding exact triple probabilities reduced mean range width from 0.015720 to 0.000579 in 1,512 Allen V1DD connections and from 0.015938 to 0.000976 in 1,438 MICrONS connections. All three- and four-contact cases became identified. A complement argument explains four-contact cases without exact half-weight ties. Allowing absolute error 0.001 in each triple probability raised mean widths to 0.004103 and 0.004673. Fourth-order constraints further narrowed, but did not remove, the remaining ranges. Solver certificates and scalar checks support these conditional results. The rates, independence constraints and size weights are assumed. One animal per map, selected incomplete arbors and no release or activity measurements limit biological claims. Original code, aggregate evidence and external retrieval steps support reproduction. No external contact records are bundled.

display.caption: Mean sharp half-loss probability range width by observed contact count and constraint mode. Failure probability is assumed to be 0.1. Lines describe allowed laws, not uncertainty across animals.
